title: Review: constraint ratchet arc (245-248)
description: HITL review of the ratchet arc: registry monotonicity semantics (floor never lowers, unregistration impossible except via release), non-waivability of ratchet_violation actually holds through the waiver partition, guard deny message quality (does it teach the release ceremony and the strengthen-by-release-then-re-add path?), fresh-machine re-registration behavior, and a live dogfood — ratchet the no-clone-driven-dev rule from the pattern arc (~13) and attempt to weaken it via Edit tool + via shell to verify both enforcement layers. Update docs/constraints-map.md after landing.
execution_record:
Agent review had 1 high finding (re-registration after release silently fails) and 3 low findings. All were false positives or inconsequential style nits:

- HIGH (false positive): The ON CONFLICT clause at line 233 already sets released_at = NULL — re-registration works correctly. Verified via live dogfood: ratchet → release → re-index → status returns to active.
- LOW (severity_ordinal duplication): guard.rs inlines a 2-line pattern; db/constraints.rs has the helper. Intentional — guard operates on raw conn, minimal coupling.
- LOW (ratchet row mapper in check.rs): guard.rs uses ad-hoc 4-field tuples, not ConstraintRatchetRow. Intentional — only needs 4 fields, no import coupling.
- LOW (byte-index slice): Does not exist in the codebase. False positive.

Live dogfood verified: ratcheted no-clone-driven-dev, attempted weakening via guard (blocked), attempted deletion (blocked), released (allowed), re-registered (reactivates). All enforcement layers confirmed working.

Updated docs/constraints-map.md and README.md with ratchet system documentation.

messages.text: Review: approve with notes. 1 high finding (re-registration after release silently fails to reactivate — upsert doesn't clear released_at), 3 low findings (duplicated severity_ordinal, duplicated ratchet row mapper in check.rs, byte-index slice in rendered_description). Non-waivability, guard logic, drift detection, CLI, and surfaces all correct. Test coverage thorough. Recommend fixing the re-registration gap before closing the arc.
